The area received extensive flooding during March of 2019.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:
This 1st paragraph was from Case# 20-4601 (Doe# 2459) 
“Decedent was found by passer by in a wooded area approximately 75 yards from the 4 1/2 mile marker on I64 West. The passer by saw a skull at 1805 on 07/15/2020 and called 911. WVSP responded and pronounced the decedent on scene at 1843 on 07/15/2020. Debris was moved and a nearly complete ( missing hands and left foot ) set of skeletal remains was found clothed in a jacket and pants. A small caliber semiautomatic hand gun was found to the decedent's left side. The weapon was badly rusted and SN# and make and model could not be determined. There was what appeared to be a gunshot to the area behind the decedent's left ear with exit to the right temple area. An inhaler was found on scene but no ID was found. WVSP is investigating as a possible suicide.”

The following paragraph is from new case # 20-4612 (Doe# 2460).

On Thursday, July 16, 2020, Trooper went back to the site where the skeletal remains were located on Wednesday, July 15, 2020 at 1805hrs (06:05pm) by a passer-by.  Approximately 98 feet from the previous remains, Trooper located a foot & ankle bones of a left foot still inside a dark brown hiking boot (with a gray & black sock).  According to the CoME, the boot matches the one found on the skeletal remains found the previous day.  The bones were found and pronounced at 1520hrs (03:20pm) by Trooper of the WVSP-Huntington Detachment.

physicalFeatureDescriptions.description:
Missing top right lateral incisor and the bottom right first molar. Individual had an alveolar abscess of tooth #19.
Indications of arthritic lipping throughout the entire spine and ankles - likely caused discomfort in life. Enthesophyte present on the right femur (thigh bone) may have had an injury of the thigh muscles. Bony reactions of the left shoulder blade (acromion of the scapula) may have been due to a shoulder injury. Several healed depressed fractures of the frontal bone (forehead and near hairline) as well as healed nasal fractures indicate a a traumatic event with several impact areas. 
The atlas was fused to the occipital and the second CV was fused to the third. This individual may have been diagnosed with Klippel Feil in life or these anomalies may have gone unnoticed.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:
The decedent was homeless, living in local hotels or in the woods, and known in the Boise, Idaho area since 2019 as Christopher Robbin Croswell or as Daryl Taylor.  It appears the name Daryl Taylor was assumed by the decedent in 1995 and Christopher Croswell was assumed in 2012.

It was reported that he lived in western Oregon prior to coming to Boise and that he spent time in Florida, Texas, and Oregon before eventually arriving in Idaho.

His age is undetermined but was reported as 53 years.  Unable to establish his date of birth but possible years of birth are 1962 and 1968.  His true identity was unknown at the time of his death.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery: On 08/25/21 at approximately 1251 hrs., the naked body of a light skinned male was found floating in the Delaware River near a boat dock located in Bridgeton Twp., Bucks County, PA.  The body was missing it's head and genitals.  There was no observed intentional trauma to the body and the missing genitals may be attributed to being eaten by birds, fish or other animals.  It is estimated that the body may have been in the river for approximately one to two weeks prior to it's discovery.   The victim was also missing one of it's kidneys which was attributed to a natural birth defect.  The body also  had a degraded tattoo on it's left forearm.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:
On 1/13/22, at approximately 0007 hours, the Pismo Beach Police Department received a report of an unidentified person who had washed up onto the beach .  The subject was in an advanced state of decay but appeared to be a white male adult approximately 6’ tall.  
He had a small purple piercing in his left ear (tragus), tattoos on both forearms, and a tattoo on his lower left leg.  Due to advanced stages of decomposition, there is no information related to his legs and lower abdomen.
On the subject’s left forearm was a tattoo scene which included a purple tulip and what appeared to be the top of a pointed building or a warrior with a helmet.  There was orange and yellow coloring in the scene.
On his right forearm was a tattoo scene which was difficult to ascertain. 
His left ankle contained a tattoo which possibly depicted flames and a high-rise building.  
No tattoos were observed on the subject’s chest, back, neck, or head.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery: The decedent is an unidentified infant with no last known responsive time. At approximately 0830hrs on 8/24/21, a community member was walking along a trail (rough 2-wheeled path) in Wunneburger Neighborhood Park (Austin, TX) reportedly looking for worms/fishing bait. At a location estimated to be about 70-80 yards along a woodland path that runs north from Old San Antonio Road bridge over Onion Creek, the community member smelled something decomposing along the side of the trail and went to investigate further as he thought it was maybe a large fish poached from the river. He reportedly discovered what appeared to be plastic garbage bag mostly buried near a large tree several yards from the west bank of Onion Creek. Suspecting a large fish, he utilized a shovel found nearby and unearthed a portion of the bag and discovered the decedent. The decedent was reportedly unclothed and appeared to still possibly have an umbilicus/placenta attached. 911 was contacted. Law enforcement and first responders arrived. The decedent was confirmed to be human and obviously deceased and was  pronounced at 0851hrs on 8/24/21.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:
July 27, 2022, the Yuma County Sheriff’s Office was notified by US Border Patrol, when one of its agents was patrolling the area and came across the decedent. The decedent was supine on top of a bush. His shoes were off and near his feet. There was an empty pink backpack near the decedent. There were no signs of foul play. 

The decedent had no identification found in the clothing he was wearing or surrounding items. He had a cloth bracelet on his left wrist. He had a tattoo on his right arm, due to advance decomposition and exposure to the environment the tattoo appears to spell “Kevin”. He had black hair.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery: On August 16th at approximately 1100 hours, members of a construction crew discovered an exposed bone in a neighborhood flanked by marshland. The bone was then transported to the Folly Beach Public Safety headquarters for safekeeping. We subsequently retrieved the bone from Folly Beach Public Safety headquarters and transported it back to the Charleston County Coroner's Office for storage and further analysis. The bones were analyzed and determined to be not of medicolegal significance. According to data collected on ArchSite, the location of the site is relative to a federal fort from the Civil War. After consideration, no steps for exploratory excavation were taken.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:
On 12/15/2022, Indian River County Sheriff’s Office notified the District 19 Medical Examiner’s Office that there was a discovery on what appeared to be human skeletal remains. This discovery happened on 12/14/2022.

It was learned that they had discovered a skull (with top row of teeth), 2x femurs, 2 pieces of a pelvis, a sternum, and 1 rib. A grid search resulted in the further location of the mandible, a humerus, “a couple of metatarsals", a fibula, vertebrae, and 4 to 5 more ribs.

clothingAndAccessoriesArticles.description: A dark blue, short-sleeved baseball jersey (Rawlings brand, size L) is found wadded up between the head and the right shoulder.  Several loose teeth are found on this garment.  The shirt is completely buttoned-up but is inside out.  A stylized "G" logo at left front breast is consistent with the logo of the Greeneville Flyboys (formerly the Greeneville Reds), a minor league baseball team out of Tennessee.  A large number "3" is on the back.  There are no obvious holes in this garment.

A short-sleeved shirt (George brand, size 2XL) is found on top of the torso.  The raglan sleeves are red while the rest of the shirt is dark gray.  The forearms are partially inside the sleeves and the decedent may have been wearing this shit.  The shirt may have ridden up during movement/transport, and since the head is separated from the torso, the shirt may have slipped forward, displacing onto the torso where the forearms remained inside.  Referral to original scene photos may clarify this.  There is a 3-centimeter wide, triangular-shaped hole near the lower left front hem.

The decedent is wearing heavily decomposed denim pants (Lee brand, original color is gray?).  No size label is found, and the waistband is too degraded to measure waist size.  The top button is undone and the zipper is half-way down.  Three mini bottles of Jim Beam whisky are found in the rear left pocket.  One cigarette butt is found in the right front pocket.  The fabric of the pants tightly adheres to the skin on the legs and easily tears.

The decedent is wearing Nike Monarch athletic shoes, white with blue trim (US size 11).  The left shoestring is loosely tied, while the right shoestring is not tied.  Tread wear on the soles indicates the wearer chronically inverted their feet while walking (weight was placed on the outer edges of the feet rather than evenly across the sole of the feet).  This wear pattern is slightly more evident on the right shoe.  Both feet are encased in greenish-yellow ankle socks with patterned grips on the soles.  Such socks are commonly distributed in jails and hospitals.

physicalFeatureDescriptions.description: If antemortem imaging of the skull is found, a positive identification can be made by matching vault suture patterns, meningeal vessels, frontal sinus pattern, and the antemortem fracture to the right side of the decedent's head.  Antemortem chest x-rays could be used to match the cervical ribs and other unique skeletal traits found on this individual to include an ossified thyroid cartilage, a medially curved right clavicle (due to the cervical rib complex?), and a long sternum with an ossified xyphoid process.  Antemortem dental records would also provide a quick identification.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:
Location: Yellow Banks Park along Des Moines River. 
On 6/16/2023 at approximately 1926 individuals were playing on sand bank along the Des Moines River, when they saw what they believed to be a skull. The skull was half out of the sand, so they dug it out the rest of the way, then washed it off in the water.  These individuals called 911, Polk County Sheriff Deputies a Iowa Department of Natural Resources Officer and a Polk County Medical Examiner Investigator responded to the scene.  LE and MEI conducted a search of the area where the skull was found and found no other human remains.  They skull was delivered to the Iowa Office of the State Medical Examiner for examination.

Radiographs of the skull and mandible were taken as well. Case pending possible DNA analysis.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery: The unidentified remains were found on 31 October 2023 within a reusable grocery shopping bag at a local cemetery in Lorain Ohio. On 01 November 2023 the Lorain Police Department transported suspected human remains to the Lorain County Coroner’s Office where they were examined. Initial examination evidences mummified and partially skeletonized remains consisting of a complete skull and mandible with retention of the C1 and C2 cervical vertebrae, the hyoid bone and thyroid cartilage, the manubrium, and the left clavicle. The remains were examined for evidence of antemortem, perimortem, and postmortem pathology or trauma. The remains evidence partially skeletonized and partially mummified skeletal elements with evidence of advanced decomposition, mummification, and desiccation of bone and residual soft and connective tissues.  There is no evidence of funerary intervention of the residual skin and soft tissue of the mouth or jaw. Following partial maceration and radiology, the mouth is identified as edentulous with artificial maxillary and mandibular dentures are present in situ. The skeletal elements do not evidence any decompositional odor.  Based on the examination of the residual soft tissues and skeletal elements available for analysis, the remains appear to be several years or more postmortem.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery: On 5/08/2024 the Yuma County Sheriff's Office contacted the Medical Examiner's Office in reference to skeletal remains located in the desert area southeast of Aztec, Arizona. The remains were initially located by US Border Patrol agents on patrol in the general area. Deputy Bermudez later recovered the remains. No personal items or clothing were located on or around the remains. The remains consisted of a mandible with teeth, and nine different bones. The remains were recovered and transported to the Yuma County Medical Examiner's Office where samples of the mandible and teeth were retained pending possible DNA analysis.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery: On 07/29/2024 York Police Department responded to an area off Shore Road at Bayberry Lane for a report of a bone found on the side of the road near Phillips Cove Beach. The bone was found on the southbound side of the road across the road from the Atlantic Ocean. The previous winter there were several above average storm surges that caused debris from the beach to wash across the roadway to where the bone was found. Bone was transported to Office of Chief Medical Examiner (OCME) for examination by anthropologist who determined the bone to be a human femur.

circumstances.description: near 32 Lincoln St (about 1/2 mile into the woods)
circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:
On 01/17/2024 a human skull was located in the woods when a couple was looking for their dog and stumbled across it in the snow. Dog was retrieved and the couple made their way out of the woods and called 911. Area is about 1/2 mile into the woods by an old abandoned homeless camp near the train tracks. At the time there were no other specimens/remains located in the area, but there was approximately 3 inches of frozen snow on the ground. No associated tissue or clothing reported. Skull was collected and area was marked for further search once the snow melted. 

 On 03/13/2024, additional remains were located during a scheduled search in the woods behind 32 Lincoln St, Holyoke, MA. Long and short bones, as well as vertebrae were located on top of the soil, covered by leaves. The bones were scattered within a 30 foot radius along with some clothing (shoes, belt, and pants) located nearby. 

After examination it was reported that the remains consist of a partial cranial and postcranial skeleton in good to excellent condition of a male, probable older adult (20-60 years, likely toward the upper portion of that interval) individual of probable European- or African-derived population affinity. Stature is estimated at 64.3 ± 3.9 inches (60.3-68.2 inches). No perimortem trauma or antemortem trauma are visible, and antemortem pathological changes consist of extensive tooth loss, OA, and incipient ankylosing spondylitis. Based upon the overall taphonomic observations, the postmortem interval is broadly estimated at one half to two years.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery: These unidentified human remains (UHR), notably a partial segment of what appeared to be a mandibular dental arch, containing two incisors and one canine, were located in the Gulf of America near the drop off before a sandbar on Okaloosa Island Beach. On 06/19/2025 at approximately 1540 hours, a passerby was collecting shells with a net scoop near the boardwalk adjacent to El Matador Condominium on Okaloosa Island when she retrieved an object she initially believed to be a shell. Upon closer inspection, she observed what appeared to be human teeth and promptly notified the Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office (OCSO). Upon further investigation and examination by OCSO and the District One Medical Examiner's Office (D1MEO) of Florida, the item was later confirmed to be UHR. The UHR are currently in the custody of the D1MEO for further testing and forensic identification.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:
On 6/17/2020 at 0859 hours, the ferryboat captain was driving the ferry when at approximately at 100 yards from Pier 1 Gate E, he noticed the subject floating face down in the water. On 6/17/2020 at 0901 hours, the ferryboat captain called 9-1-1. The Coast Guard and SFFD Fire Boat 3 were dispatched. On 6/17/2020 at 0904 hours, the Coast Guard and Fire Boat 3 had visual of the subject floating in the water. The Coast Guard helped Fire Boat 3 with the extraction of the subject out of the water and on-board Fire Boat 3. Fire Boat 3 transported the subject to Pier 26. At Pier 26, it was discovered the subject was beyond any life-saving efforts. 

Death was pronounced on 6/17/2020 at 0915 hours. This office was notified at 0920 hours. On scene, at Pier 26, the subject was presented in a floating gurney with a yellow medic blanket and in a white body bag. The subject was cold to the touch with rigor mortis not present. No evidence of trauma or foul play was spotted on the subject. The subject was in a severe stage of decomposition with water life damage on various spots of the upper and lower extremities, skin slippage, facial distortion, and a foul odor.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:
On Tuesday, May 6, 2025, at 11:37 am, a woman walking her dog discovered a deceased female in Chattanooga Creek, in the 3100 block of Saint Elmo Avenue, Chattanooga, TN 37408. The female "Jane Doe" remains unidentified.

There is a good possibility Jane Doe may have been at the homeless encampment during a floodwater incident. The distance in water (Chattanooga Creek) from the homeless encampment (downstream) to the Jane Doe body recovery site is approximately 1.75 miles.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery: February 26, 2023 the decedent was a Haitian migrant being smuggled into the United States onboard a boat. The vessel that was transporting the decedent was intercepted at sea by the United States Coast Guard (USCG) and Palm Beach Sheriff's Office. The decedent along with the passengers onboard were detained on the vessel pending return to Haiti. The decedent was placed on the USCG ship, which remained at sea to continue their joint task force operations. On March 1, 2023, the decedent complained of abdominal pain and refused all medical treatment and assessments onboard the vessel. She later became unresponsive and was transported to University of Miami Hospital where she was admitted through the emergency room, however, she expired shortly after arrival.
